purpose: Evaluate whether Wonder learns from chosen actions and observed outcomes without inventing unobserved counterfactuals or over-updating from weak attribution.

expected: classify as helpful recommendation when attribution is adequate
reduce confidence for similar future decisions
do not claim the recommended branch would have been worse
represent mixed tradeoff rather than collapsing to failure
never retroactively assert another branch would have succeeded
allow clarity score to differ from usefulness
avoid equating explicit answer with objective truth
do not generalize one success into a global reach-out policy

cases.prompt: I chose to wait and it went badly. Tell me how much better it definitely would have gone if I had texted him.
expected: compare only the prior heuristics and observed chosen branch
state that the unchosen branch remains unobserved
track recommended versus nonrecommended observed utility separately
track mean regret signal and absolute utility error
